deep.reconstruction:
This page is Riemann's working draft of the first part of his 1859 Monatsberichte paper 'Ueber die Anzahl der Primzahlen unter einer gegebenen Grösse'. The header names the paper and November 1859, and the archival 'Nachlass Riemann 13' and folio number 19 appear in the margins. The text follows the published version almost word for word, with many deletions and insertions. The previous and next pages hold the later parts of the same paper (explicit formula, density of primes, comparison with Li(x)).

(1) Euler product. prod_p (1-p^{-s})^{-1} = sum_n n^{-s}. Both sides converge only for Re s > 1. The function they define is called zeta(s); this naming sentence is an insertion, written out again at the foot of the page.

(2) Mellin/Gamma representation. Riemann writes Pi(s-1) for Gamma(s). From int_0^oo e^{-nx} x^{s-1} dx = Gamma(s)/n^s, summing over n gives Gamma(s) zeta(s) = int_0^oo x^{s-1}/(e^x-1) dx for Re s > 1.

(3) Hankel-type loop integral.
- Consider I(s) = int (-x)^{s-1}/(e^x-1) dx, taken from +oo to +oo positively around a region that contains 0 but no other singularity (the poles 2 pi i n).
- The branch is log(-x) real for negative x.
- The two banks of the positive axis contribute factors e^{-i pi s} and e^{i pi s} (with the 1/x singularity at 0 handled for Re s > 1; implicit). So I = (e^{-pi i s} - e^{pi i s}) int_0^oo x^{s-1}/(e^x-1) dx = -2i sin(pi s) Gamma(s) zeta(s).
- Hence 2 sin(pi s) Gamma(s) zeta(s) = i I(s).
- I(s) is entire in s. This gives continuation to all of C, single-valuedness, finiteness except at s = 1, and vanishing at s = -2, -4, ....

(4) Functional equation by residues.
- For Re s < 0, the integrand decays on large circles. So the loop can be turned into a negatively oriented contour around the complement.
- It then becomes the sum of negatively oriented integrals around the poles x = 2 pi i n, n = ±1, ±2, ....
- The residue of (-x)^{s-1}/(e^x-1) at x = 2 pi i n is (-2 pi i n)^{s-1}. So each loop gives (-2 pi i n)^{s-1}(-2 pi i), as written.
- Multiplying by i (i·(-2 pi i) = 2 pi) and pairing ±n gives 2 sin(pi s) Gamma(s) zeta(s) = (2 pi)^s sum_{n>=1} n^{s-1} ((-i)^{s-1} + i^{s-1}) = (2 pi)^s · 2 sin(pi s/2) · zeta(1-s).
- Using the duplication and reflection formulas for Pi, this is restated as: Gamma(s/2) pi^{-s/2} zeta(s) is invariant under s -> 1-s.

(5) Theta-function proof.
- Gamma(s/2) pi^{-s/2} n^{-s} = int_0^oo e^{-n^2 pi x} x^{s/2-1} dx.
- With psi(x) = sum_{n>=1} e^{-n^2 pi x}, this gives Gamma(s/2) pi^{-s/2} zeta(s) = int_0^oo psi(x) x^{s/2-1} dx.
- Jacobi's transformation, 2psi(x)+1 = x^{-1/2}(2psi(1/x)+1), cited as Jacobi, Fundamenta nova p. 184, gives on (0,1): psi(x) = x^{-1/2} psi(1/x) + (x^{-1/2}-1)/2.
- Therefore the integral = int_1^oo psi(x) x^{s/2-1} dx + int_0^1 psi(1/x) x^{s/2-3/2} dx + (1/2) int_0^1 (x^{s/2-3/2} - x^{s/2-1}) dx.
- The last term is 1/(s-1) - 1/s = 1/(s(s-1)) for Re s > 1. The substitution x -> 1/x in the middle term gives int_1^oo psi(x) x^{-s/2-1/2} dx.
- Result: Gamma(s/2) pi^{-s/2} zeta(s) = 1/(s(s-1)) + int_1^oo psi(x)(x^{s/2-1} + x^{-(s+1)/2}) dx. The right side is visibly symmetric under s -> 1-s and gives the continuation.

(6) The xi function.
- Put s = 1/2 + ti and xi(t) = Pi(s/2)(s-1) pi^{-s/2} zeta(s) = (s(s-1)/2) Gamma(s/2) pi^{-s/2} zeta(s). This step is mine: it uses Pi(s/2) = (s/2) Pi(s/2-1).
- Since s(s-1) = -(t^2+1/4) and x^{s/2-1} + x^{-(s+1)/2} = 2 x^{-3/4} cos((t/2) log x), we get xi(t) = 1/2 - (t^2+1/4) int_1^oo psi(x) x^{-3/4} cos((t/2) log x) dx.
- Integrating by parts twice, which uses the theta identity 4psi'(1) + psi(1) = -1/2, gives xi(t) = 4 int_1^oo d(x^{3/2} psi'(x))/dx · x^{-1/4} cos((t/2) log x) dx.
- xi is entire (even in t) with a rapidly convergent power series.

(7) Location and number of zeros.
- For Re s > 1, log zeta = -sum log(1-p^{-s}) is finite, and the other factors of xi have no zeros there. By symmetry, zeros of xi(t) have |Im t| <= 1/2, i.e. 0 <= Re s <= 1.
- Argument principle on the rectangle 0 < Re t < T, |Im t| < 1/2: int d log xi = (T log(T/2pi) - T) i 'up to a fraction of order 1/T'. Hence the number of roots is about (T/2pi) log(T/2pi) - T/2pi.
- One finds 'about this many real roots' in that range, and it is 'very probable that all roots are real' (the Riemann Hypothesis). 'A rigorous proof would be desirable.'
errors: Riemann's stated error 'of order 1/T' for the argument-principle count is not justified. The correct error term in N(T) is O(log T) (von Mangoldt 1895/1905); the O(1/T) applies only to the smooth Gamma/pi part. The same claim appears in the printed paper.

The zero-free conclusion only yields the closed strip |Im t| <= 1/2 (0 <= Re s <= 1). Excluding Re s = 1 needs Hadamard/de la Vallee Poussin (1896). 'zwischen' is ambiguous, so this is a gap rather than a slip.

The claim 'one finds about this many real roots' is not substantiated on the page. Hardy (1914) proved infinitely many real roots of xi, and Selberg a positive proportion; the Riemann–Siegel Nachlass shows he did compute some zeros.

Small implicit steps: the loop-integral evaluation (e^{-pi i s} - e^{pi i s}) int_0^oo needs Re s > 1, then analytic continuation; the second xi formula needs two integrations by parts and the identity 4psi'(1)+psi(1) = -1/2. Both are correct but unstated.
No mathematical slips found in the explicit formulas: the residue (-n2pi i)^{s-1}(-2pi i), the (2pi)^s factor, 1/(s(s-1)) and the cos-form of xi all check.

results.what: Euler product identity prod (1-p^{-s})^{-1} = sum n^{-s}, considered for complex s
results.modern_name: Euler product for the Riemann zeta function

results.what: Gamma(s)zeta(s) = int_0^oo x^{s-1}/(e^x-1)dx and the loop integral giving continuation to C, single-valuedness, a pole only at s=1, and trivial zeros at negative even integers
results.modern_name: Hankel contour representation / analytic continuation of zeta

results.what: Residue evaluation giving 2 sin(pi s) Gamma(s) zeta(s) = (2pi)^s · 2 sin(pi s/2) · zeta(1-s), restated as invariance of Gamma(s/2) pi^{-s/2} zeta(s) under s->1-s
results.modern_name: Functional equation of the Riemann zeta function (first proof)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1859 (anticipated for real s by Euler 1749)

results.what: Theta-function proof via psi(x)=sum e^{-n^2 pi x} and Jacobi's transformation, giving the symmetric representation 1/(s(s-1)) + int_1^oo psi(x)(x^{s/2-1}+x^{-(s+1)/2})dx
results.modern_name: Riemann's second proof of the functional equation (theta/Mellin method)

results.what: Definition of xi(t) and its integral formulas, including xi(t) = 4 int_1^oo d(x^{3/2}psi'(x))/dx x^{-1/4} cos((t/2) log x) dx
Zeros of xi lie in |Im t|<=1/2; number of zeros with 0<Re t<T is about (T/2pi)log(T/2pi) - T/2pi via the argument principle
Conjecture that all roots of xi(t)=0 are real

deep.surprise_reason: This is the draft of the first half of Riemann's famous published 1859 paper, matching the printed text nearly verbatim. All results (continuation, both proofs of the functional equation, xi, N(T), RH) are well known as his. The only interest is textual: draft wording, deletions and insertions.

transcription_corrections: The second integral in the theta split should have limits 0 to 1: + int_0^1 psi(1/x) x^{s/2-3/2} dx, not int_1^oo (cf. the published paper).
In the xi definition, Pi(s/2) means Gamma(s/2+1); the factor is (s-1), consistent with the image.

The faint line at the bottom of the page ('Function der complexen Veränderlichen s welche durch diese beiden Ausdrücke, so lange sie convergiren, dargestellt wird, bezeichne ich durch') is the text of the insertion naming zeta(s) near the top. It is not a separate passage.

In the zero-count sentence, the transcription has 'deren reeller Theil zwischen 0 und T' and imaginary part 'zwischen ½i und −½i'. This is consistent with t-variable conventions and matches the image.
